title: Fat Bass — approximate factory recreation
method: Source-only FFT shows the recurring 43.65 Hz F1 family. Connected sections rise to 51.9 Hz Ab1, and the higher slide around 4.0 s settles near 77.8 Hz Eb2 then 87.3 Hz F2. On/off estimates follow the isolated waveform attacks and abrupt endings. Adjacent notes overlap by 8 ms to trigger the approximate legato glide; no original MIDI overlap is claimed.
uncertainties: ESTIMATED MIDI: original performance MIDI is unavailable. Notes, onsets, note-offs and overlaps are interpretations of the source MP3, not recovered original events.
Velocity 100 is an explicit constant placeholder, not an estimate of the original key velocities. Note-off velocity is 64. No original controller or pedal events have been recovered.
The factory parameter dump is unavailable. The companion patch is a newly authored approximate recreation, not exact factory SysEx; an exported SysEx file encodes this approximation only.

Audio frequencies do not uniquely reveal played key numbers: original oscillator tuning, octave switches and system transpose are unknown. The MIDI and companion patch jointly choose an octave interpretation.

Times are measured from decoded source MP3 audio; encoder delay, hardware response latency and prior effect state are not removed. Timing is approximate, generally 20–40 ms; short transitions can be less certain.
The opening and higher-slide destination pitches are relatively clear; exact glide trajectories and whether they came from portamento or pitch bend are unknown.
The filter movement may have been performed manually. The LFO is an approximation and will not duplicate its trajectory. No community same-name patch was used.

patch_design.name: APX FatBass
rationale: A saw bass with low-frequency boost and a 24 dB low-pass approximates the asymmetric low waveform and strong first few harmonics.

Short release preserves the nearly silent gaps; overlapping notes and short legato glide approximate the connected slides. The preview glide settled more slowly than the source, so the raw time was reduced from20 to14.
A gentle slow filter LFO stands in for the source brightness changes across repeated F notes.

Preview spectrum was much brighter than the isolated opening hardware bass. A 24 dB low-pass and reduced base cutoff suppress the excess upper harmonics; slow sinusoidal cutoff movement remains an authored proxy for the changing source brightness.
uncertainties: All voicing values are authored approximation parameters, not measured or recovered Roland factory parameter values.
The opening and higher-slide destination pitches are relatively clear; exact glide trajectories and whether they came from portamento or pitch bend are unknown.
The filter movement may have been performed manually. The LFO is an approximation and will not duplicate its trajectory. No community same-name patch was used.
